raw_text:
Below is a conservative, cardiac‑rehab–informed 12‑week general fitness program designed for a 58‑year‑old male, six months post‑MI, cleared for moderate intensity only. Priorities: aerobic capacity, total‑body strength/endurance, mobility/balance, and confidence with gym routines while strictly avoiding Valsalva, maximal effort, and keeping HR < ~70% age‑predicted max (~115 bpm). Emphasis on rate of perceived exertion (RPE 4–6/10), steady nasal/controlled breathing, and longer rest as needed.

Global guidelines
- Frequency: 4 days/week (2 cardio-focused, 2 mixed strength + light cardio). Optional gentle mobility on off days.
- Intensity: HR ≤ 115 bpm; RPE 4–6/10. Able to speak in full sentences.
- Breathing: Exhale on exertion for every rep; avoid breath holding.
- Warm‑up: 8–10 minutes every session (5–7 min light cardio + dynamic mobility).
- Cool‑down: 5–10 minutes light cardio + long exhales; finish with easy stretches.
- Progression: First progress duration, then volume, then light load; never increase two variables in the same week. If HR creeps above target or RPE >6, back off.
- Red flags (stop and refer): Chest pain/pressure, unusual shortness of breath, dizziness, palpitations, excessive fatigue that doesn’t resolve with rest, edema, or BP >180/100 during exercise.

Monitoring
- Use HR monitor. Measure BP pre‑session first 2–3 weeks if available.
- Track session RPE and note any symptoms.
- 2–1 rule: Two consecutive days feeling “off” → reduce next session volume by 25–50%.

Structure overview (12 weeks)
- Phase 1 Foundation (Weeks 1–3): Technique, tolerance, steady aerobic base.
- Phase 2 Build (Weeks 4–6): Add time and light resistance; introduce intervals at low–moderate effort.
- Phase 3 Consolidation (Weeks 7–9): Slight volume increase, light circuit density, balance/core emphasis.
- Phase 4 Maintenance & Confidence (Weeks 10–12): Solidify routine, small variety, prepare for independent training.

Session templates
- Cardio day: Warm‑up → steady or gentle intervals → cool‑down.
- Strength/mobility day: Warm‑up → full‑body 6–8 exercises → optional 5–10 min very easy cardio finisher → cool‑down.

Exercise selection notes
- Machines and cables preferred early for stability; progress to free weights as tolerated.
- Big patterns: squat/hinge, push, pull, carry, core anti‑rotation/anti‑extension, calf/ankle work, balance.
- Tempo: Controlled 2–3 s down, 1–2 s up, continuous breathing.

Week‑by‑week plan

Phase 1: Foundation (Weeks 1–3)
Goals: Establish routine, perfect breathing, tolerate 30–40 min sessions without symptoms. RPE 4–5.

Week 1
- Cardio A (e.g., treadmill walk or recumbent bike)
  • 5–7 min warm‑up, easy pace
  • 15 min steady state at HR 95–110 bpm (RPE 4–5)
  • 5–8 min cool‑down
- Cardio B (elliptical with arms or bike)
  • 5–7 min warm‑up
  • 3 x 4 min easy‑moderate + 2 min very easy between (keep HR ≤115)
  • 5–8 min cool‑down
- Strength Day 1 (machines/cables)
  • Leg press (high seat) 2x12
  • Seated row 2x12
  • Chest press 2x12
  • Bodyweight box squat or goblet to box (very light) 2x10
  • Cable pulldown (wide or neutral) 2x12
  • Cable Pallof press 2x8/side
  • Standing calf raise 2x12
  • Farmer carry with light DBs 2 x 20–30 m (normal breathing)
  Rest 60–90 s; RPE per set 5/10.
- Strength Day 2 (variation)
  • Hip hinge: cable pull‑through or light RDL 2x10
  • Lat‑focused: supported DB row 2x12/side
  • Push: incline machine press 2x12
  • Knee‑dominant: step‑up to low box 2x10/side
  • Shoulder: cable face pull 2x12
  • Core: dead bug or bird dog 2x6–8/side
  • Balance: tandem stance 2x30–45 s
  Optional 5 min very easy bike before cool‑down.

Week 2
- Cardio A: 18–20 min steady (same HR/RPE)
- Cardio B: 4 x 4 min easy‑moderate + 2 min very easy
- Strength Days: Increase to 3 sets on 2–3 main movements; keep others at 2 sets. Same reps, RPE 5–6. Add light rear‑foot support for split squat if tolerated (2x8/side).

Week 3
- Cardio A: 22–24 min steady
- Cardio B: 5 x 3 min easy‑moderate + 2 min very easy
- Strength Days: Most moves 3x10–12; maintain technique focus. Add light cable anti‑rotation walkout 2x6/side. Introduce seated overhead press machine 2x10 if BP/HR stable.

Phase 2: Build (Weeks 4–6)
Goals: Reach 25–30 min cardio, build total‑body strength endurance. Introduce gentle intervals. RPE 5–6 max.

Week 4
- Cardio A (treadmill/bike): 25 min steady, HR 100–112
- Cardio B: 6 x 3 min easy‑moderate + 2 min very easy
- Strength Day 1 (3 sets unless noted)
  • Leg press 3x12
  • Seated row 3x12
  • Chest press 3x10–12
  • Step‑up (medium box) 3x8/side
  • Face pull 2–3x12–15
  • Pallof press 3x8/side
  • Carry: suitcase carry 2x20–30 m/side
- Strength Day 2
  • Cable pull‑through 3x10–12
  • Supported DB row 3x10/side
  • Incline press 3x10
  • Goblet squat to box 3x8–10
  • Lat pulldown 3x10–12
  • Bird dog 3x6–8/side
  • Calf raise 2–3x12–15

Week 5
- Cardio A: 28–30 min steady
- Cardio B: 4 x 4 min easy‑moderate + 3 min very easy
- Strength: Same exercises; progress by +1–2 reps or slight load only if RPE ≤5 and HR stable. Add hip abduction/adduction machines 2x12 if needed for hip stability. Include 5 min cool‑down walk after strength.

Week 6
- Cardio A: 30 min steady
- Cardio B: 5 x 4 min easy‑moderate + 2–3 min very easy
- Strength: Introduce light circuit format on Day 2 to improve density without raising HR:
  • Circuit (3 rounds, 6 stations, 45 s work/30–45 s transition): leg press, chest press, seated row, step‑up, cable pull‑through, face pull. Keep breathing continuous; RPE ≤6.

Phase 3: Consolidation (Weeks 7–9)
Goals: Maintain HR control with modestly higher density; improve balance and core. RPE 5–6.

Week 7
- Cardio A: 32–35 min steady
- Cardio B: 8 x 2 min easy‑moderate + 2 min very easy (shorter bouts to manage HR)
- Strength Day 1 (traditional sets)
  • Goblet squat to box 3x10
  • Chest press 3x10–12
  • Seated row 3x10–12
  • Romanian deadlift (light) 3x8–10
  • Lat pulldown neutral grip 3x10
  • Pallof press 3x8/side
  • Farmer carry 2x40 m
- Strength Day 2 (balance/core emphasis)
  • Split squat (supported) 3x8/side
  • Incline press 3x10
  • Single‑arm cable row 3x10/side
  • Hip hinge: cable pull‑through 3x10–12
  • Lateral step‑down to low box 2–3x8/side
  • Dead bug 3x8/side
  • Balance: single‑leg stance near support 2x20–30 s/side

Week 8
- Cardio A: 35 min steady
- Cardio B: 6 x 3 min easy‑moderate + 2 min very easy
- Strength: Keep loads constant; add a 4th set on one lower and one upper movement if RPE ≤5 and HR stable. Maintain long exhales on effort.

Week 9
- Cardio A: 30–32 min steady with light incline or cadence variation (only if HR allows)
- Cardio B: Fartlek style 20–25 min: 1 min slightly faster + 2 min easy, repeat; ensure HR stays below cap by extending easy segments as needed.
- Strength: Circuit day reintroduced (6 stations x 3 rounds, 40 s work/30–45 s transition) with same movements; keep HR ≤115.

Phase 4: Maintenance & Confidence (Weeks 10–12)
Goals: Solidify habits, slight variety, independent pacing. RPE 5–6. Emphasize symptom‑free completion over progression.

Week 10
- Cardio A: 35–38 min steady
- Cardio B: 5 x 4 min easy‑moderate + 3 min very easy or 30 min continuous on a different modality (rower only if form and BP stable; keep stroke light).
- Strength Day 1
  • Leg press 3–4x10–12
  • Chest press 3x10–12
  • Seated row 3–4x10–12
  • Step‑up 3x8–10/side
  • Face pull 2–3x12–15
  • Pallof press 3x8/side
- Strength Day 2
  • Goblet squat to box 3x8–10
  • Incline press 3x10
  • Single‑arm cable row 3x10/side
  • RDL (light) 3x8–10
  • Lat pulldown 3x10–12
  • Dead bug or side plank (elevated) 2–3x20–30 s/side

Week 11
- Cardio A: 38–40 min steady
- Cardio B: 10 x 2 min easy‑moderate + 2 min very easy
- Strength: Maintain volumes; swap in new but similar options to keep engagement (e.g., machine fly for chest press, chest‑supported T‑row for seated row). Do not chase load; maintain RPE 5–6 and HR control.

Week 12
- Cardio A: Client’s preferred modality 35–40 min steady, symptom‑free
- Cardio B: Choice day: either gentle intervals (6 x 3 min + 2 min easy) or low‑incline continuous walk 30–35 min
- Strength: Full‑body circuit (6–7 stations x 3 rounds, 45 s work/30–45 s transition), then finish with 5–10 min easy cardio. Review form and create go‑forward plan.

Warm‑up template (every session, 8–10 min)
- 5–7 min easy walk/bike/elliptical
- Dynamic mobility: ankle rocks, hip openers, thoracic rotations, banded shoulder external rotations, 6–8 reps each
- Breathing rehearsal: 3–4 slow diaphragmatic breaths; practice exhale on exertion cue.

Cool‑down and mobility (5–10 min)
- 3–5 min light walk/bike
- Gentle stretches: calves, quads/hip flexors, hamstrings, pecs, lats. Hold 20–30 s, easy breathing.

Load and progression rules
- Start very light (approx. 30–50% of estimated 1RM or a load you could lift for ~18–20 reps). Perform only prescribed reps with 4–5 reps “in reserve.”
- Progress only if:
  • HR and BP remain within targets
  • RPE ≤5–6 and technique pristine
  • No next‑day undue fatigue or soreness >24–36 hours
- When progressing: first add time (cardio), then sets/reps, then slight load (2–5 lb upper body, 5–10 lb lower body).

Nutrition and recovery
- Hydration: 500–750 ml water in the 2 hours pre‑session; sip during; rehydrate after.
- Pre‑exercise: light snack 60–90 min pre‑workout (e.g., yogurt with fruit, small oatmeal, or a banana with a few nuts) to avoid hypoglycemia.
- Daily diet: Emphasize heart‑healthy pattern (Mediterranean‑style): vegetables, fruits, legumes, whole grains, nuts, olive oil; fish 2x/week; limit saturated fat, added sugars, excess sodium and alcohol. Coordinate with physician if on statins/antihypertensives.
- Protein: ~1.0–1.2 g/kg/day unless contraindicated; spread across meals for recovery.
- Sleep: Aim 7–8 hours; avoid strenuous late‑evening sessions if they elevate HR near bedtime.
- Medication timing: If on beta‑blockers or nitrates, rely more on RPE and talk test than HR; confirm timing with physician to prevent exercise‑induced hypotension.

Safety and technique reminders
- No Valsalva: continuous breathing; coach with “exhale through the effort.”
- Avoid positions or grips that provoke dizziness or chest discomfort.
- Use slow transitions (e.g., from floor to stand) to prevent BP drops.
- Keep sessions in a cool, well‑ventilated area; avoid extreme heat/humidity.

Outcome expectations
- By Week 12: Comfortable with 35–40 min cardio at HR <115 bpm, improved stamina and daily activity tolerance; full‑body strength endurance with 3–4 sets of 8–12 at light–moderate loads; better balance and confidence. Continue this structure beyond Week 12, progressing time or slight resistance only while staying within medical guidance.
